newsitem.title: BELGIUM: How the EU will decide who qualifies for EMU.
newsitem.headline: How the EU will decide who qualifies for EMU.

text.p: European Union countries are due to decide in early 1998 which among them will join their planned monetary union (EMU) on January 1, 1999.
The following is the procedure as laid out in the Maastricht Treaty:

-- The European Commission and the European Monetary Institute will report to the ECOFIN, the council of economy and finance ministers, on how each member state fared in 1997 in meeting the criteria laid down for EMU entry.
-- The ECOFIN will vote on each country, using the EU's qualified majority voting procedure. The result will be sent to a summit of EU leaders for a final, consensus, decision.
-- Under qualified majority voting, each country has a weighted vote, loosely related to its size.
-- There are 87 votes in total. Sixty-two votes are needed for a qualified majority, meaning that if a group of countries can come up with 26 votes, they can reject or block the report.
-- The breakdown means - in theory - that the "Club Med" countries of Italy, Spain, Portugal and Greece could stop EMU if they believed they were being unfairly left out.
-- Conversely, a "hard core" group of Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, Austria and Luxembourg could stop EMU if they thought countries that did not deserve to qualify were about to be let in.
